title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E506 is Euler's commentary on Lagrange's method for integrating dx/√X = dy/√Y, where X = A+Bx+Cx²+Dx³+Ex⁴ and Y is the same polynomial in y. On the preceding pages Euler writes Lagrange's integral as V²/(x−y)² − D(x+y) − E(x+y)² = Δ, with V = √X+√Y. He then checks it by differentiating it directly.

On the previous page he found the dx-part, −dx/((x−y)³√X)·(M√Y+N√X), where
- M = 4A+B(3x+y)+2C(x²+xy)+D(x³+3x²y)+4Ex³y,
- N = 4A+B(x+3y)+2C(y²+xy)+D(y³+3xy²)+4Exy³.

This page completes the dy-part. The dy-coefficient is (1/√Y)[Y'V/(x−y)² + 2V²√Y/(x−y)³ − D√Y − 2E(x+y)√Y]. Using V²√Y = (X+Y)√Y + 2Y√X, it splits into two groups.
- The √X-terms are √X(Y'(x−y)+4Y)/(x−y)³. Expanding gives exactly N.
- The √Y-terms are √Y(Y'(x−y)+2(X+Y)−D(x−y)³−2E(x+y)(x−y)³)/(x−y)³. Expanding gives exactly M.

Euler obtains both identifications by the x↔y, sign-change symmetry with the dx computation.

§8: Adding the two parts gives (dy/√Y − dx/√X)·(N√X+M√Y)/(x−y)³ = 0. Dividing out the common factor recovers the proposed equation. So the integral is correct for every value of Δ, which is therefore a genuinely arbitrary constant: the integral is complete.

§9–10: As a warm-up for applying Lagrange's method in full generality, Euler takes the rational case dx/(a+2bx+cx²) = dy/(a+2by+cy²). He introduces Lagrange's auxiliary variable t with dx/dt = X and dy/dt = Y. On the next page this yields the algebraic, complete integral XY/(x−y)² = C.
errors: None in the mathematics. I verified by explicit expansion that Y'(x−y)+4Y = N and that Y'(x−y)+2(X+Y)−D(x−y)³−2E(x+y)(x−y)³ = M, including the E-terms: 2(x+y)(x−y)³ = 2x⁴−4x³y+4xy³−2y⁴.
Printed 'effecti' should be 'affecti' (terms affected by √Y); this is a typographical slip.
On the next page the printed '(ddx/dx dt) X'' lacks the '=' sign (also 'dy/dt Y'). These are typographical only.

ideas.what: Direct verification of Lagrange's algebraic integral of the Euler differential equation dx/√X = dy/√Y with quartic X, by differentiation. The derivative factors as (dy/√Y − dx/√X)(N√X+M√Y)/(x−y)³.
ideas.modern_name: Euler's addition theorem for elliptic integrals; algebraic first integral of the Euler equation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (1750s, addition theorem); Lagrange (1766–69, Misc. Taurinensia, method via auxiliary time variable)
ideas.where_published: E506 itself (Acta Acad. Sci. Imp. Petrop. 1778 II, publ. 1781); related verifications appear in Euler's Institutiones calculi integralis vol. 1 and E251/E345-type papers on the addition theorem

ideas.what: Observation that the constant Δ remains arbitrary, so the algebraic integral is complete (general).
ideas.modern_name: complete (general) integral / one-parameter family of solutions

ideas.what: Rational warm-up case dx/(a+2bx+cx²) = dy/(a+2by+cy²), handled by Lagrange's time parametrization. It leads to the integral XY/(x−y)² = C.
ideas.modern_name: Riccati/Möbius-invariant first integral; quadratic (degenerate) case of the addition theorem

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine algebraic verification page in a well-known, published and commented-on paper on Lagrange's integration of the Euler equation. All results are standard and correctly credited.
transcription_corrections: 'effecti erunt' is as printed but should read 'affecti erunt'.
The image reads 'methodum Grangianum'; the transcription is consistent.
In §8 the printed bracket '(N√X + M√Y' is missing its closing parenthesis before the division by (x−y)³; the transcription has silently corrected this.
